DEFINITION · qeva:1:information@2

Self-information

Self-information assigns a logarithmic surprise to an event of positive probability.

editorialinformation-theory · probability
Trace this conceptSearch connections

PLAIN

The idea

Within a probability model, a less probable event carries more self-information when surprise is measured logarithmically.

EXACT

The compact statement

For an event E with 0<P(E)≤1 and a real base b>1, its self-information is I_b(E):=−log_b(P(E)). The unit is the bit when b=2 and the nat when b=e.

Example

Either result of a fair coin toss has self-information 1 bit.

Boundary / caveat

Self-information is model-relative and is not identical to meaning, knowledge, usefulness, evidence, or truth.

Assumptions

  • A probability space and an event E of positive probability are fixed. · Probability space @1

Historical links

Provenance

Adds b>1 and disambiguates self-information from the much broader word information. This is an original QEVA formulation and remains subject to independent review.
